title: PRA updates interim prudential treatment of tokenised assets, stablecoins and other cryptoasset exposures
summary: On 18 May 2026 the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) wrote to Chief Executive Officers of banks and designated investment firms, superseding its 2022 letter on cryptoasset exposures. It reaffirms that firms must keep applying the full prudential framework -- the PRA's Fundamental Rules, Pillar 1, ICAAP and Pillar 2 -- including a 100% capital requirement for unbacked cryptoassets under the market risk framework. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision has published an international cryptoasset-exposure standard and started an expedited review of targeted elements on an unconfirmed timeline; firms may use the standard's classification conditions where PRA rules allow discretion, but the PRA expects to consult on a proposed future framework only 'in 2028 at the earliest.' Tokenised traditional assets, including Digital Securities Sandbox and Digital Gilt Issuance Pilot instruments, should generally get the same treatment as non-tokenised equivalents where the legal rights conferred are identical and the underlying risks are comparable.
why_it_matters: For someone new to UK bank regulation, this letter is the Bank of England's Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) telling banks how much capital they must hold against cryptoassets they hold themselves: a conservative 100% capital charge still applies today to unbacked cryptoassets. It also signals that certain lower-risk cryptoassets and tokenised traditional assets can already get more favourable, risk-sensitive treatment under the PRA's existing rules where these allow discretion, informed by an international Basel standard that has already been published but is still under a targeted review -- though the PRA does not expect to consult on its own proposed future framework before 2028 at the earliest.
